payload.entry: listen-manifest done in sase-listen checkout. Baseline: reproduced bob-cli-bq — flush_pending dropped the outbox entry after _push_episode succeeded without calling mark_manifest_published, so the source library manifest kept published:false. Fix (src/sase_listen/feedhost.py): flush_pending takes library and passes it to _push_episode; on success it calls mark_manifest_published(episode_id, library) before dropping the outbox. A mark failure (OSError/ValueError) keeps the outbox entry via queue_publish and lands in failed with a 'delivered but the source manifest could not be marked published' error, so nothing is lost silently — surfaced by publish --pending's existing failure output. publish_any now threads its library into its best-effort flush_pending call. Tests (tests/test_feedhost.py, 4 new): success marks both manifests + empties outbox + second flush is a no-op; failure (missing MP3) keeps outbox and published:false; mixed batch splits correctly; monkeypatched mark failure stays queued. Docs: docs/multi-machine.md Outbox paragraph notes the new mark-on-retry behavior. Gate: sase tool run check (ruff + format + mypy --strict + codespell + full pytest) succeeded. Limitation: repo has no reconcile command, so the three stale Athena manifests (outbox already empty, feed already has the episodes) need a manual one-time repair per episode id with the repo venv: python -c "from sase_listen.feed import mark_manifest_published; mark_manifest_published('<episode-id>')". Leaving bob-cli-bq open for the lander to verify/close.

flush_pending now marks the source manifest published on successful retry (library threaded through push+mark; mark failures stay queued and reported). 4 new tests in tests/test_feedhost.py; sase tool run check green. bq left open for lander verification; no reconcile command exists so the three stale Athena manifests need the manual one-shot repair recorded in the phase note.

payload.entry: Root cause: footerClauses(for:) in Sources/RefsCore/RefsPDFUpdates.swift never yields a clause for coordination_timeout (busy) holds — only refreshedOpen notes and reading/changed holds. The test fixture at RefsPanelModelTests.swift:2286 built a busy-only receipt, so pdfUpdateFooterClauses was [] by design and XCTAssertFalse(isEmpty) failed. This predates the test: identical code since 9fb67f3, test unchanged since 72cd721, and the banner-only busy contract is documented in docs/refs.md:408 and encoded by passing tests testPDFUpdateSurfaceSetsFooterClausesAndBusyBanner and RefsPDFUpdatesTests.testSurfaceHidesNotificationsWhenVisibleOrDisabledAndDedupesBusyHolds. Fix is fixture-side (production code and docs contract are correct): added a savedFirst refreshed note (ref/papers/open.md) to the receipt, realistic for a Highlights save that refreshed one open PDF while another stayed busy. Assertions unchanged in strength. Evidence: just portable-check exit=0 (1648 tests, 0 failures, Linux Swift 6.0.3); mac scratch copy bundle.sh exit=0 and just typecheck-tests exit=0 (all test targets PASS incl. BobMacCaptureTests), scratch removed. Limitation: mac has Command Line Tools without XCTest so CI must execute the test; watch macOS CI on the landed SHA containing bob-mac-capture Tests/RefsPanelModelTests.swift with the saved-note fixture.
